title: SLO matrix for maintenance windows, model-fallback priorities, and progressive error budgets
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Produce a single, implementable SLO matrix and rollout guardbook that covers: (1) scheduled maintenance windows (nightly regional upgrades and monthly major kernel deployments), (2) model-fallback prioritization when primary model variants exceed error budgets, and (3) progressive error-budget exhaustion behavior across duty cycles. This ticket will produce acceptance criteria, monitoring signal definitions, a staged rollout plan for enforcement automation, and docs for on-call runbooks. Scope: - SLO targets for interactive chat and batch embeddings across customer tiers (Free, Standard, Enterprise). - Error budget burn-rate policies tied to regional maintenance windows. - Model-fallback order (same-architecture quantized variant -> smaller architecture -> fallback to higher-latency cached responses) with explicit quality regressions allowed per tier. Out of scope: Per-customer contractual SLA negotiation (handled by Account Owning PM). Deliverables: 1) SLO matrix table (p50/p95/p99 latency bands, availability target, acceptable quality regressions) as text ready for Console configuration. 2) Rollout gating rules and automation pseudocode for canary/fallback triggers. 3) On-call playbook snippets and alert thresholds for early warning. 4) Acceptance criteria and observability dashboards links.
acceptance_criteria: A1: SLO matrix defined and approved: p50/p95/p99 latency bands and availability targets per workload and tier (Free/Standard/Enterprise)
A2: For each SLO, an 'error budget burn-rate' policy is specified (normal, maintenance, emergency) with numeric thresholds and linked alert IDs
A3: Model-fallback ordering documented with measurable quality-allowance per fallback step and mapping to Console fallback policy flags
A4: Rollout gates defined so that a canary rollout is automatically halted if burn-rate > 4x sustained over 10m or if p99 latency increases > 30% vs baseline
A5: Playbook examples added to on-call runbook and reviewed by SRE and Runtime teams
A6: Dashboards created in Grafana with panels for the SLOs and burn-rate windows; links included in ticket
A7: Implementation owners (runtime, routing, console) assigned and timeline agreed in next weekly sync
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - Canary: 1% traffic -> monitor 30m. Abort if burn-rate > 3x or p95 > 2x baseline.
Gate 1 - Limited ramp: 10% traffic -> monitor 1h. Abort if burn-rate > 2x sustained over 15m or error rate increase > 1% absolute.
Gate 2 - Regional ramp: 50% traffic in region -> monitor 3h. Abort if p99 increases > 25% or availability drops below regional target.
Gate 3 - Global: 100% traffic -> monitor 6h. Abort and trigger rollback if error budget exhausted for Enterprise tier or global burn-rate > 4x.

Maintenance exception: During scheduled maintenance windows defined per region, error-budget thresholds relax by a factor (maintenance multiplier = 1.5) but must be disclosed on status page and in console metadata.
monitoring_signals: latency_p50/p95/p99 by model and route (per-tenant where applicable)
error_rate (5xx-like and model-decoder failures) with cause labels
burn_rate computed over sliding 1h and 24h windows
model_quality_regression signal: distribution shift on token-level perplexity and sample-based eval metrics
prefix cache hit ratio and kv-cache tail latency
downstream routing fallback counters (counts of requests routed to fallback variants)
implementation_notes: Runtime: add burn-rate evaluator hook and expose per-route SLO metrics. Routing: implement declarative fallback order in routing table with priority weights and tie to fallback-quality metadata. Console: represent SLO matrix and allow tenants to opt into relaxed maintenance windows. SRE: add new alert IDs and dashboard panels; draft runbook snippets. Plan: - Week 1: finalize SLO matrix and signal spec. - Week 2: instrument burn-rate and fallback counters in staging. - Week 3: implement rollout automation in canary service. - Week 4: run cross-team canary and QA, prepare release notes.
